subject: Fwd: Northpeak Search — request for Dedicated burst capacity commitment (timeline + what we can promise)

body:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 12, 2025 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Fwd: Northpeak Search — request for Dedicated burst capacity commitment (timeline + what we can promise)
Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Burst_Option_OnePager_v3.pdf, Burst_Denial_Reasons_CheatSheet_v2.pdf

Team — escalating because this is now a late-stage item for Northpeak’s Dedicated signature.

They’re asking for (a) what we can promise for burst availability (regions/hardware), (b) when, and (c) whether “burst is guaranteed” during their scheduled indexing windows.

I can sell “guardrailed / subject to fleet safety,” but they want something they can take to procurement and to their VP Eng.

Can you please respond with:
1) Current planned GA date + what we’ll say externally if it slips
2) What we can commit to (or explicitly cannot) around scheduled burst windows
3) Regions/hardware we’ll support at GA (at least us-east H100 is fine)
4) Any contract language guidance (Michael)

Target: I need an answer I can copy/paste to customer today.

Forwarded context below.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Sales Enablement (NA)
Redwood Inference


---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@northpeaksearch.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 12, 2025 at 8:41 AM PT
Subject: Dedicated Burst Capacity — commitment needed for final approval
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Devon Li <devon.li@northpeaksearch.com>

Hi Stephanie,

We’re aligned on Dedicated baseline sizing. The remaining blocker is Burst.

For our weekly indexing jobs we need the ability to temporarily exceed our reserved capacity (in-region) for 2–4 hours at a time. Our procurement/legal team is asking for clarity on:

- When Burst Capacity will be generally available
- Whether burst capacity is “guaranteed” during a scheduled window vs. best-effort
- What happens when the platform denies burst (expected error codes / behavior)
- Which regions / hardware classes are supported at launch (we’re starting in us-east)

If you can share what you can commit to contractually (even at a high level), we can unblock final signature.

Thanks,
Asha
VP Engineering, Northpeak Search



From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 12, 2025 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Fwd: Northpeak Search — request for Dedicated burst capacity commitment (timeline + what we can promise)

Thanks, Steph. Here’s a crisp external answer you can use; Michael/Laura/Jordan please chime in on contract wording / dates.

Product position (external-safe):

- GA timing: Target GA is June 2025 (staged by region/hardware). Prior to GA we can support limited beta access for select Dedicated customers starting May 2025.
- What burst is: Burst lets a Dedicated tenant temporarily exceed baseline by borrowing from Redwood-managed burst pools in the same region/hardware class, subject to admission control and fleet safety limits.
- What we can/can’t promise: We can commit to providing the *feature* and agreed tenant-level burst limits, but we cannot guarantee that 100% of burst requests will be admitted during a given window (admission is always subject to real-time pool saturation and global safety circuit breakers).
- What happens if denied: Requests are handled deterministically; if burst is denied, Redwood returns an explicit denial reason and the system falls back to baseline behavior (or returns an overload/429 depending on the configured policy). We’ll share the expected denial reason codes + recommended retry/backoff behavior.

For Northpeak specifically: If they need a “scheduled window” guarantee, the right commercial construct is either (a) increasing baseline reservation for that window (permanent or a separate reserved add-on), or (b) we treat the event as a pre-planned capacity request (not initial GA scope, but we can operationally coordinate if we have notice). I’d avoid promising “guaranteed burst” in a shared pool.

Let me know their required burst ratio vs baseline (e.g., 1.5x for 4 hours weekly). That determines if beta is feasible in us-east.

Lauren Bishop
Product, Dedicated
Redwood Inference


From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 12, 2025 at 10:26 AM PT
Subject: Re: Fwd: Northpeak Search — request for Dedicated burst capacity commitment (timeline + what we can promise)

+1 to Lauren’s framing. Contractually, I’d strongly avoid any “guaranteed burst” language unless we’re actually reserving GPUs for them (which changes the economics and the nature of the product).

Suggested language you can paraphrase for the customer (non-redline version):

- “Burst Capacity is an optional feature that may allow Customer to temporarily exceed its Dedicated baseline capacity by utilizing Redwood-managed burst pools, subject to availability, platform safety controls, and applicable usage limits.”
- “Burst Capacity is not a reserved capacity commitment and may be throttled or denied to protect platform reliability and other tenants.”
- “Dedicated baseline SLA remains unchanged; burst usage is best-effort and excluded from latency/throughput commitments unless explicitly stated in an Order Form.”

If Northpeak insists on a scheduled guarantee, we should offer a commercial alternative: baseline reservation increase or a separate reserved increment for that period.

Michael Grant
Legal (Commercial)
Redwood Inference


From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 12, 2025 at 11:01 AM PT
Subject: Re: Fwd: Northpeak Search — request for Dedicated burst capacity commitment (timeline + what we can promise)

From pricing/packaging standpoint, please avoid committing to “guaranteed burst during scheduled windows” under the shared burst pool construct.

What we *can* commit to commercially in the order form (once we know their baseline and burst ratio):
- Tenant-level burst cap (e.g., “up to +X GPUs equivalent” or “up to 1.5x baseline”), and
- A maximum monthly burst spend cap / burst usage limit so they have cost predictability.

If they need guaranteed additional capacity during indexing, the right lever is increasing baseline reservation for the period (or adjusting baseline upward permanently). That’s clean and financeable.

Laura Bennett
Finance
Redwood Inference


From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 12, 2025 at 12:18 PM PT
Subject: Re: Fwd: Northpeak Search — request for Dedicated burst capacity commitment (timeline + what we can promise)

Steph — this is exactly the right escalation.

Guidance for what you can promise (leadership-approved positioning):

1) Timeline: “Target GA June 2025; limited beta earlier for select Dedicated customers.” Don’t provide day-level dates. If pressed: “We will provide at least 30 days notice if our target GA timing materially changes.”

2) Availability: For launch, we should message “staged by region/hardware” and only name what we’re confident in. If Northpeak is us-east only, keep it to that.

3) Guarantees: Do not promise guaranteed burst admission. We can promise: transparency (denial reason codes), guardrails that protect baseline SLOs, and ability to set hard caps.

If Northpeak is signing now contingent on a guarantee, route them to reserved baseline expansion. If they’re okay with “best-effort burst, within agreed caps,” we can proceed.

Jordan Blake
VP, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference


From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@northpeaksearch.com>
Cc: Devon Li <devon.li@northpeaksearch.com>
Date: Wed, Mar 12, 2025 at 2:06 PM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated Burst Capacity — commitment needed for final approval
Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Burst_Option_OnePager_v3.pdf, Burst_Denial_Reasons_CheatSheet_v2.pdf

Hi Asha (cc Devon),

Totally understood — here’s the clearest commitment we can make today.

Timeline / availability
- We are targeting general availability for Dedicated Burst Capacity in June 2025, rolling out in stages by region/hardware.
- We can support a limited beta for select Dedicated customers prior to GA; given your starting region is us-east, we can review eligibility for beta access as soon as we have your baseline + desired burst ratio.

What “burst” means (and what it is not)
- Burst allows your Dedicated deployment to temporarily exceed baseline capacity by borrowing from Redwood-managed burst pools in the *same region/hardware class*, subject to real-time admission control and fleet safety limits.
- Burst is not a reserved capacity guarantee. Admission can be throttled/denied if pool saturation or platform safety controls trigger.

If burst is denied
- You will receive explicit denial behavior (e.g., overload/429 with structured reason codes). We also provide recommended retry/backoff guidance.

If you need a guaranteed window
- If you require guaranteed extra capacity during a scheduled indexing window, the appropriate mechanism is increasing your reserved baseline capacity to cover that window (rather than relying on shared burst pools). We can help you size that.

Two quick questions so I can propose a concrete plan:
1) What baseline are you planning to reserve (e.g., # of GPUs or tokens/sec target)?
2) For the weekly indexing window, what’s your desired burst ratio and duration (e.g., 1.5x for 4 hours)?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sales Enablement (NA)
Redwood Inference


From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@northpeaksearch.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Devon Li <devon.li@northpeaksearch.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 13, 2025 at 9:22 AM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated Burst Capacity — commitment needed for final approval

Thanks Stephanie — this is helpful.

We can accept best-effort burst (with transparency) as long as baseline SLOs are protected.

For sizing: baseline would be equivalent of 8x H100 in us-east. Indexing peak would like up to 1.5x–2.0x for 3 hours, once per week (usually Tue 02:00–05:00 PT).

Procurement may ask for one sentence in the order form noting burst is “targeted GA June 2025” and available earlier for beta in us-east if mutually agreed.

Can you confirm that’s acceptable?

Asha


From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@northpeaksearch.com>
Cc: Devon Li <devon.li@northpeaksearch.com>
Date: Thu, Mar 13, 2025 at 4:02 PM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated Burst Capacity — commitment needed for final approval

Asha — yes, that’s acceptable with the right wording.

We can include an order form note along these lines:
“Customer may elect to enable the Dedicated Burst Capacity feature when generally available (target June 2025), subject to Redwood’s staged rollout by region/hardware and applicable availability and safety controls. Beta access in us-east may be made available earlier by mutual agreement.”

Separately, we’ll size baseline to protect your steady-state requirements, and burst will be capped (and metered) so you have both performance and cost predictability.

If you’d like, I can join a 15-min procurement call to walk through the “best-effort burst / baseline protected” concept and the denial reason transparency.

Best,
Stephanie
